title: A section of an integral birational morphism is an isomorphism
statement: Let $X$ and $Y$ be integral schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme]. Let $f:Y\to X$ be separated [def-weil-proper-morphism], and suppose there is a nonempty open $V\subseteq X$ such that $f^{-1}(V)\to V$ is an isomorphism. If $s:X\to Y$ is a section, meaning $f\circ s=\mathrm{id}_X$, then $s$ and $f$ are inverse isomorphisms. In particular, the section maps the generic point of $X$ to the generic point of $Y$ [def-sc-generic-point].

source.place: Tag 0BFP, lemma-modification-normal-iso-over-codimension-1, last closed-section paragraph of proof (4); Schemes Tag 01KT (lemma-section-immersion).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-section-separated-closed-immersion] to $f:Y\to X$ and its section $s$. Its hypotheses are precisely separatedness of $f$ and $f\circ s=\mathrm{id}_X$. Thus $s$ is a closed immersion. In particular its image $C=s(X)$ is closed in $Y$, and $s$ is a monomorphism (cancel maps into $s$ using the left inverse $f$).

Put $W=f^{-1}(V)$. The isomorphism $W\to V$ and nonemptiness of $V$ imply $W\ne\varnothing$. For $y\in W$ put $x=f(y)\in V$. The section identity gives $f(s(x))=x$, hence $s(x)\in W$; injectivity of $W\to V$ gives $s(x)=y$. Therefore $W\subseteq C$. Integrality of $Y$ implies irreducibility [def-pc-integral-scheme]. If $C\ne Y$, the proper closed sets $C$ and $Y\setminus W$ would cover $Y$, contradicting [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Thus $C=Y$.

source.place: Tag 0BFP, lemma-modification-normal-iso-over-codimension-1, last paragraph of proof (4), closed image is all of Y; density argument made explicit.

proof.text: The scheme $Y$ is reduced by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme] to the closed immersion $s:X\to Y$ and the morphism $\mathrm{id}_Y:Y\to Y$. The required image containment holds by Step 2. We obtain $t:Y\to X$ with $s\circ t=\mathrm{id}_Y$. Consequently $t=(f\circ s)\circ t=f\circ(s\circ t)=f$, so $s\circ f=\mathrm{id}_Y$. Together with the given $f\circ s=\mathrm{id}_X$ this proves that $s$ and $f$ are inverse isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0356, lemma-map-into-reduction, applied to the identity; supplies the scheme-theoretic justification for the final Y = X in Tag 0BFP.

proof.text: Let $\eta_X$ be the generic point of $X$. By [def-sc-generic-point], $\overline{\{\eta_X\}}=X$. The inverse scheme isomorphisms just obtained induce inverse continuous maps, so $s$ is a homeomorphism on spaces. Hence $\overline{\{s(\eta_X)\}}=s(\overline{\{\eta_X\}})=s(X)=Y$, which says exactly that $s(\eta_X)$ is the generic point of $Y$.

source.place: Tag 0BFP, lemma-modification-normal-iso-over-codimension-1, generic-point assertion in the last paragraph of proof (4).
